late.text: I just got your message. It says you sent it last week. I don't know what they do with them in there.
Your message came days after you sent it. I thought something had happened.

news.text: Your aunt asked about you after church. I told her you're doing your time and doing it right.
The car's making that noise again. Don't worry about it.
I picked up extra shifts. It keeps me busy.
I moved some things into storage. Long story. I'll tell you when you're home.

signoffs.text: I love you. Eat something. Mom

checkin.text: Good to hear from you. I check that tablet every night before bed, even when I know there won't be anything.
Thank you for writing. It's been a while. I won't make a thing of it.
Nobody at the facility would tell me anything when I called. Just tell me you're all right. That's all I need.

visit.text: The drive home felt shorter than usual. You looked thinner. I'll bring quarters for the machines next time.
I'm so sorry about Saturday. I'll tell you on the phone. I'll be there next time if I have to walk.
I'll come up the Saturday after next, same as always. Tell me if anything changes on your end.
I mailed the visitor application. They said it takes time. I'm waiting like everybody else.
An hour, and I couldn't even hug you. I didn't know what to do with my hands.

money.text: I put a little on your books Friday. Don't ask where it came from. Buy yourself something real to eat.
I'll do what I can. It won't be much. Things are tight right now, but don't you worry about that.
I can't this month. I'm sorry. I'll try in a few weeks.

trouble.text: What happened? Don't tell me it was nothing. You said that when you were fifteen too.
They took time off your release, didn't they. You can tell me. I'd rather know than guess.
I read it twice. I don't know what to say anymore. I'm still here.

seg.text: Where did they move you? I kept writing and nothing came back. I kept writing anyway.
Someone at the facility said you were "off the unit." That's all they would say. Are you safe?
I saw where they have you. I'm not going to pretend I didn't. Tell me what you need.
You looked better on Saturday than you've sounded in your messages. Don't go back there.

family.text: Everyone's the same. Your cousin got a new job. The neighbors still ask about you, and I still don't know what to say.
Your aunt sends her love. She means it this time.

release.text: {monthsText}. I wrote it on the calendar in pen.
I'm counting too. I just don't say it out loud anymore.
I washed the sheets on your old bed. I know it's early. Let me have it.

sorry.text: You don't have to keep saying sorry. Just come home and be here. That's the sorry I want.
I know you are. Sorry doesn't pay for anything, but I know you are.

ink.text: Was that tattoo on your arm new? I didn't want to ask in front of the officer.

phone.text: Is that number you called me from last week still good? I tried calling it back and nobody answered.

efv.text: Should I bring the new shoes to the family visit? The ones you said you needed?

money.text: I sent the money to that name you gave me, like you asked. Tell me it got where it needed to go.

blank.text: You sent me a subject line. Just the subject. I read it anyway, and then I sat there.

late.text: Your message just came through. It's dated last week. He kept asking if you wrote.
I didn't get this until days later. I thought you were mad at me.

news.text: He lost his first tooth. He wants to mail it to you. I told him the post office doesn't take teeth.
Work cut my hours again.
He drew you a truck, because you "drive trucks for work." I didn't correct him.

checkin.text: Hey you. Long day here. He finally fell asleep on the couch, so I'm writing this with one hand.
Got your message. Things are busy. I'll write more when I can.
I called the facility and got nowhere. Write me back the second you can.

visit.text: He talked about the vending machine sandwich the whole ride home. Said it was the best one he's ever had.
It was good to see you. Just us this time. I'm still not sure that was the right call.
I'm sorry about Saturday. I'll explain on the phone. He cried in the car. I'm not telling you so you'll feel bad. You should just know.
I'm sorry about Saturday. I'll explain on the phone.
We'll come up next weekend if I can get the car back. He wants to show you he can whistle.
I'll come up next weekend if I can get the car back. Just me, like we said.
Still waiting on the approval letter. He asks every day if it came.
He asked why he couldn't sit on your lap. I didn't have an answer that wasn't a lie.
An hour, and I couldn't touch you. I don't know which is worse, that or not coming.

money.text: I'll put twenty on when I get paid. That's what I can do right now.
I can't right now. It's your books or his shoes.

trouble.text: What did you do? Please don't make this longer. He's counting days too, even if he doesn't know what he's counting.
How much longer? Just give me the number. I need to know what to tell him.

seg.text: You disappeared for weeks. Where were you? I told him your phone broke.
Seeing you there scared me. Tell me it's almost over.
You looked like yourself again on Saturday. Mostly. Don't go back there.

family.text: He's reading now. Short words. He sounded out "stop" on a sign and was so proud of himself.
He's okay. He asked why you're always at work on his birthday. I said you'd make the next one.

release.text: {monthsText}. I keep doing the math. He keeps asking when you get to stop working.
Okay. We'll figure it out when it gets here. One thing at a time.
We need to talk about what we tell him. Soon. Before you're standing in the kitchen.

sorry.text: I know. I'm not mad tonight. Ask me tomorrow.
I'm tired of sorry. I need you to not need to say it.

ink.text: Was that tattoo new? I kept looking at it the whole visit.

phone.text: Can you call me from that other number again? It was so good to hear you at night.

efv.text: Should I pack those new shoes for you for the family visit? He picked them out.

money.text: I sent twenty to that guy's cousin like you said. Why couldn't it just go on your books?

blank.text: You sent a subject and nothing else. He asked what you said. I made something up.

late.text: Your message came late. I worried, but I kept the porch light on anyway.
They held your message somewhere a while. I don't know why they need to read what you write your grandmother.

news.text: The tomatoes came in too fast this year. I gave half to the church.
My hands are bad in the mornings now. I write slower, but I still write.
The neighbor boy mows the lawn. He does it crooked, like you did.

signoffs.text: I pray for you every night. Grandma

checkin.text: I was so glad to see your name on the screen. I read it at the kitchen table twice.
I didn't hear from you, and the lady on the phone wouldn't tell me anything. Write when you can, even one line.

money.text: I sent what I could. It isn't much. Buy what you need to keep writing me.
I'm on a fixed income, you know that. But I'll find a little. I always do.

trouble.text: I won't scold you. I raised you, I know you. Keep your head down, like your grandfather used to say.
I know there's more you aren't telling me. That's all right. I knew before you told me the first time.

seg.text: You went quiet and I knew something happened. You don't have to say what. I just need to know you're eating.

family.text: Everyone's fine. Your cousins don't call me enough. Don't you be like them when you get out.

release.text: {monthsText}. I'm going to try to still be here when you get out. That's a joke. Mostly.
I'm making up your room. The quilt's on the bed already.

sorry.text: There's nothing you could do that would make me stop loving you. I raised you. I'd know.

phone.text: Was that you who called the other night? The number was strange. It was so good to hear your voice.

money.text: I sent the money to the man you told me about. I hope he's a good friend to you.

blank.text: Your message came with nothing in it. I don't know how that machine works. Write me words, even three.

late.text: Your message came late. She checks the tablet like it's Christmas, so next time send it earlier.
Got this days after you sent it. Not my fault.

news.text: She got a part in the school play. A tree. She's very serious about it.
Her teacher says her reading's better.

checkin.text: Got it. She's at practice. I'll show her when she's home.
She smiled when I told her you wrote. Just so you know.
You stopped writing and she noticed. Whatever's going on, don't let her hear it from somebody else.

visit.text: She talked about the visit all week. Thanks for keeping it about her.
I'm not getting into Saturday in here. She's fine. She's used to waiting.
I can bring her the second Saturday. Not the first. I work.
I sent in the paperwork. It's on them now.
She asked why she couldn't hug you. I told her it's the rules. She said the rules are stupid. She's not wrong.

money.text: I'm not putting money on your books. I'm raising your daughter. Ask your mom.
I can't do money. I'll print some pictures of her for you instead.

trouble.text: I don't need the details. I need you to stop making her wait longer.
Great. More time. What am I supposed to tell her?

seg.text: Your mom said you were "moved." I don't want to know. Just don't let it happen again while she's counting.
I don't want her seeing you like that again. Get yourself out of there.

family.text: She's taller. She asked again if you're a bad person. I said no. Don't make me a liar.
She's good. She wants to know if you have a window.

release.text: {monthsText}. We'll talk about the schedule when you're out. Not before.
When you get out, we do this slow. She needs slow.

sorry.text: I don't need an apology. She might, one day. Save it for her.

ink.text: She noticed the new tattoo. She asked if it hurt. I didn't know what to tell her.

phone.text: Don't call me late from random numbers. If you want to talk, use the tablet.

blank.text: You sent an empty message. If you don't have anything to say, don't send anything.

late.text: Your letter took the long way. You know how it is.
Got yours late. Somebody liked reading it.

news.text: Same here. Count, chow, count.
Moved cells. New guy snores like a truck.
Got a job in the kitchen. Don't laugh.

checkin.text: Good to hear from you. It's quiet over here, which is how I like it.
Heard you went quiet. I'm not going to ask in here. You know why.

money.text: I'd send something if I had it. You know I don't. Ask Mom, but go easy on her.

trouble.text: Don't put details in writing. You know better. Just tell me if it's handled.
Do your time. Don't let them add to it. They love adding to it.

seg.text: Been there. Count the walls, do push-ups, don't talk to the door. It ends.

family.text: Mom sounds tired when she writes. Call her if you can. I can't.

release.text: {monthsText}. Don't come back. I mean it.
When you walk out, don't look back at the fence. That's how you end up back inside it.

sorry.text: Nothing to be sorry for between us. You know who should be in here. Let it go.

phone.text: Heard you had a line out at night. Careful.

blank.text: Got a blank one from you. Nothing to say is still something to say, I guess.

late.text: {name}, your message reached me later than you sent it. I'm sorry for the wait.
It took a while to reach me. I'm glad it did.

news.text: Our group started a book drive for the library there. Tell me if any titles make it to you.
I'm helping at the food bank on Tuesdays now. It reminds me how much people carry.

checkin.text: {name}, it was good to hear from you. I hope this week was gentler than the last.
I was told you were unavailable for a while. I'm here whenever you're able to write.

visit.text: Thank you for the visit. You talked more than last time. I noticed.
I'm sorry I wasn't there this time. It wasn't for lack of wanting.
I'm planning to visit again this month if the schedule allows. Is there anything you'd like to talk about?
My visitor application is still in review. I'll keep checking.
Thank you for seeing me, even like that. You looked tired. I'll keep coming.

money.text: I'm not able to put money on anyone's books. Our program doesn't allow it. I can send a list of free programs and books, if that would help.

trouble.text: Thank you for being honest with me. That's harder than it sounds in there. What do you think happened?
I won't pretend that isn't hard news. It doesn't change what I think of you.

seg.text: Being alone that long is its own weight. If you want to write about it, I'll read every word.
I'm glad I came, even then. Write to me about it, if it helps.

family.text: How is your family? You haven't mentioned them in a while. You don't have to, but I'm asking.

release.text: {monthsText}. Have you thought about the first week? Not the whole future, just the first week.
I've put together a list of places that help people in their first month out. I'll send it to you.

sorry.text: You don't owe me an apology, {name}. But I hear you, and it matters that you said it.

ink.text: I noticed the new tattoo at our visit. I hope it means something good to you.

blank.text: {name}, your message came through with only a subject. I'm still here when you have the words.

late.text: Got your message. Later than you sent it, looks like.
This came through days late. I don't know how that works.

news.text: Still at the same place. They keep saying they'll retire me.
Fixed the gutter. Took me three days.

checkin.text: Got your message. I'm not much of a writer. I read it a couple of times, though.
Okay. I'm here.
Nothing from you in a while. I figured. You don't have to explain.

visit.text: It was good to see your face. I didn't know what to say in there. Next time I'll try harder.
About Saturday. I owe you an explanation, and I'll give it in person.
I'll come again. Tell me which Saturday works on your end.
Paperwork's in. They said wait.
Couldn't shake your hand. Funny what you miss.

money.text: I put something on your books. Don't make a thing of it.

trouble.text: I'm not going to lecture you. I lost the right to do that a long time ago.
That's more time. I'm sorry. I know that's not enough of a word.

seg.text: I spent thirty days in a cell once, in the army, for something stupid. It isn't the same. But I know a little.
Saw where they're keeping you. Didn't like it. I won't say more in here.

family.text: Not much to report. Your aunt asked about you. I said you were doing all right. I hope that's true.

release.text: {monthsText}. I could pick you up, if you want. You don't have to answer now.
I cleared out the spare room. It's yours if you want it, for as long as you need.

sorry.text: I've got my own sorry to say. Let's do it face to face.

ink.text: That tattoo on your arm. New? Didn't look like something they'd let you have.

phone.text: You called me from a number I didn't know. Is that allowed?

efv.text: I'll bring the shoes to the family visit, if they let me through with them.

blank.text: Got a message with nothing in it. I figured that was about right for us.

late.text: Sorry, just saw this. It says it came days ago.
Your message came late. I've been busy anyway.

news.text: Work's been crazy.
I moved some of your stuff into my sister's garage. It's safe there.
I've been going out more. Friends from work. It's nothing.

checkin.text: Hey. Sorry, it's been a week. Hope you're doing okay in there.
Hey you. I miss your voice. Call me when you can?
Hey. Got your message.
Didn't hear from you for a while. Figured you were busy too.

visit.text: It was good seeing you. It's a long drive. I'll try to come again.
I'm sorry about Saturday. Something came up. I should have told you.
I'll come up next month. I promise this time.
I don't know if I can make it up there this month. Work.
Still waiting to hear back on the visitor thing, I think.
That was hard, not being able to touch you. I sat in the car a long time after.

money.text: I can't right now. Maybe ask your family?
I'll put something on when I can. Things are tight.

trouble.text: Okay. I don't really know what to say to that.
Are you okay? Please just get through this.
So it's longer now? I'm trying to plan my life here.

seg.text: I didn't know they could just do that. Are you okay now?
That sounds rough.
I didn't know they could keep you like that. Is it over soon?

family.text: Everyone's fine, I think. I haven't really seen your family in a while.

release.text: {monthsText}. Okay. We should talk when it's closer.
{monthsText}. I've been thinking about it a lot.
We should talk before you get out. Like, really talk.

sorry.text: I know. It's not just you. It's everything.
You don't have to be sorry. I just miss how things were.

phone.text: Was that you calling at two in the morning from that number? Don't do that. I have work.

money.text: I sent it to that name like you said. That's the last time, okay?

blank.text: You just sent the subject? Okay.

late.text: Your message came through like a week late. They reading your mail to me?
Just got this. Took its sweet time.

news.text: Same crew, same corner, same everything. You're not missing much.
Ran into your old manager. He asked about you.
Got a new car. Well, new to me.

checkin.text: What's good. Nothing changes out here, which is good and bad.
You went ghost on me. Whatever it is, I'm still here.

visit.text: Good seeing you. You look stronger. Don't get too big in there.
My bad on Saturday. Long story. I'll make it up to you.
I'll come through next visiting day. Tell me if you need anything.
Still waiting on them to approve me. Guess my record's not helping.
No dap, no hug, nothing. Like visiting a fish tank. You hanging in?

money.text: Put something on your books today. Don't worry where it's from.
I'm short this month. Next one, for sure.

trouble.text: Keep your head down. You got people waiting on you.
That's more time? Don't let them keep you. Seriously.

seg.text: The hole? Damn. You good now? Write me something real when you can.
Saw you in there. That's no way to live. Hold on.

family.text: Everybody's good. I check on your people when I can.

release.text: {monthsText} and you're out. We're getting food first. Real food.
I'll be at the gate. Don't even argue.

sorry.text: Sorry for what? You'd do the same for me. You already did.

ink.text: Yo, that new tattoo is clean. Who did it?

phone.text: Hit me again from that number. Late night's good.

money.text: Sent the money to your boy's people like you said. All good.

blank.text: You sent me a blank message, bro. You good?

late.text: This came days after you sent it. I almost wrote you something mean before it showed up.
Got it late. Of course.

news.text: The little one has an ear infection. Third one this year.
Work moved me to graveyard. I sleep while they're at school.
The oldest got a B in math. I didn't even help.
Work moved me to graveyard. I sleep all day now, and I still can't sleep.
The house is too quiet. I keep their room the way it was.

checkin.text: Got your message. Read it on my break. Everyone's alive. That's the update.
Got it. I'm too tired to write much.
Two weeks and nothing. Are you okay or not? Just tell me.
Two weeks and nothing. The kids asked. I said you were busy. Are you okay or not? Just tell me.

visit.text: The kids talked about the visit for days. The little one wants to know why you can't come home with us.
It was good to see you. I didn't know what to do with my hands without the kids there.
About Saturday. I'm not doing this in a message. I'll explain on the phone.
I can bring them next month if I can get a Saturday off. No promises.
I'll come up next month if I can get a Saturday off. No promises.
Still waiting on the approval. I filled out the form twice because I messed up the first one.
The kids didn't understand why they couldn't hug you. Neither did I.
An hour, and I couldn't hug you. I didn't know that's how it would be.

money.text: I don't have it right now. I'm sorry. I really don't.
I don't have it right now. I'm sorry. Everything I have is stretched over them.
I put ten on. That's what I've got. Don't buy junk with it.

trouble.text: Are you serious. Okay. What happened? Not the version for Mom.
How much longer? I need the real number.
How much longer? I need the real number. I'm planning their whole year around it.
I can't carry your trouble too. I'm sorry. I just can't.

seg.text: You went quiet. Is it over? Don't put the details in writing. Just tell me if it's over.
I saw where they have you. Just tell me when it's over.
You looked tired on Saturday, but you looked like you. Keep it that way.

family.text: The kids are okay. They fight, they eat, they grow out of their shoes.
The oldest asked if you're coming to the school thing. I said maybe. Don't make me a liar.
The caseworker says they're doing fine. That's all she'll tell me. I hate that it's all she'll tell me.

release.text: {monthsText}. I'm not counting yet. I'll count when it's close.
We need to talk about where you're staying. Before you're out.
We need to talk about where you're staying. And about the kids. Before you're out.

sorry.text: I know. Me too. For all of it.
I know you mean it. I'm just tired.
Sorry doesn't pick them up from school. I know you mean it. I'm just tired.

ink.text: Was that tattoo new? You know Mom's going to see it.

phone.text: What was that number you called from? It came up unknown. Call me from it again.

efv.text: Do you want me to bring those shoes to the family visit, or will they take them at the door?

money.text: I sent the forty to the person on that paper you gave me. Who is that, anyway?

blank.text: You sent me a subject line. That's it? I'm working doubles and you send me a subject line.

late.text: Got your message late. Didn't know they slow them down like that.
This came days after you wrote it, says here.

news.text: The old block's different now. They tore down the corner store.
Saw some of the old crowd. Not all of them made it.

checkin.text: Good to hear back. Didn't know if you would.
Didn't hear from you a while. Hope you're alright.

visit.text: Wild being in there, even just for a visit. Good to see you, though.
Sorry about the visit. Something came up.
I could come by some weekend if that's cool.
Still waiting on the visitor approval. Takes forever.
Didn't know it'd be like that. Couldn't even shake your hand.

money.text: I can do a little, once. Don't make it a habit.

trouble.text: Damn. Keep your head down in there.
That sounds bad. Hope it doesn't add on.

seg.text: That's rough. Didn't know they still did that.
That place they had you in. Rough.

family.text: Can't say I know much about your people these days. Haven't been around.

release.text: {monthsText}. That's not bad. Let me know when you're out.
Almost there. Call me when you're out.

sorry.text: Nothing to apologize to me for. We were young.

phone.text: Was that a cell you called me on? I didn't know you could do that in there.

blank.text: Got your message. There was nothing in it.

late.text: Your message came late. They're reading it, you know that. Write accordingly.
Took a week to get here. Some things never change.

news.text: Got a job at a warehouse. Pays every two weeks. Felt strange at first, getting a check.
First time I went to a grocery store, I stood in the cereal aisle for ten minutes. Too many choices.

checkin.text: Good to hear from you. Out here it's a different kind of hard. In there, just do the day in front of you.
You went quiet. I know what that usually means. Hope you're out of there.

visit.text: Strange sitting on the other side of that table. Good to see you.
Sorry about visiting day. My PO had me jumping through hoops. I'll try again.
I'll come through again when I can. My PO knows about it.
They're still checking me out. Somebody who's been inside waits longer. Figures.
No-contact. I remember those. You'll be back on the floor soon. Hold on.

money.text: I'll put a little on. Don't owe anybody in there. That's the real advice.

trouble.text: Don't let them build a file on you. Every write-up follows you out.
They'll keep adding if you let them. Walk away from it, even when it costs you.

seg.text: The hole messes with your head. Read anything you can get. Count something. It ends.
I saw the unit they've got you in. Do that time with your head, not your fists.

family.text: Do you talk to your people? Do it now. It's harder after.

release.text: {monthsText}. Start planning now: ID, a place to sleep, a phone. The first week is the hardest.
When you walk out, have somebody waiting. If nobody is, call me.

sorry.text: Don't apologize to me. Apologize to whoever's still waiting on you. I never did, and I wish I had.

phone.text: Don't call me from that number again. You know better. They listen.

money.text: I sent what you asked to that name. Be careful with that.

blank.text: Blank message. I remember doing that. Don't let it get that way.

late.text: Your message came days after the date on it. Is that normal?
Sorry for the slow reply. Yours took a while to arrive!

news.text: I started a garden. Mostly I'm growing weeds.
My cat knocked my coffee onto the keyboard. She's not sorry.

checkin.text: I always get a little nervous before I open your messages. In a good way.
I didn't hear from you for a while and got worried. I hope everything is okay.

money.text: I'm not able to send money, I'm sorry. I hope that's okay. I can keep writing, though.

trouble.text: That sounds really hard. I don't know much about how it works in there. Do you want to tell me?
Does that mean more time? I'm sorry. That seems so unfair.

seg.text: I looked up what that means. I'm sorry. I hope it's over.

family.text: Do you have family who writes you? You don't have to answer that.

release.text: {monthsText}! What's the first thing you want to do?
Almost there. I'm really happy for you.

sorry.text: You don't have to apologize! I'm just glad we write.

blank.text: Your message was empty. Did something go wrong? I hope you're okay.
